title: At the Doctor
grammarNote: 'Doler' and similar verbs work backwards from English: the body part is the subject and the person takes an indirect object pronoun (me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies). Duration is expressed with 'desde hace' or 'llevo + time + con...', unplanned mishaps use accidental 'se' (se me torció el tobillo), and advice or obligation is framed with 'tener que', 'deber', and 'hay que'.

phrases.target: Me duele la cabeza desde hace tres días
phrases.native: My head has hurt for three days
phrases.phonetic: meh DWEH-leh lah kah-BEH-sah DES-deh AH-seh tres DEE-as
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Doler' works backwards: the body part ('la cabeza') is the grammatical subject, and 'me' marks who feels the pain.

exampleSentence.target: Me duele la cabeza desde hace tres días, doctor.
exampleSentence.native: My head has hurt for three days, doctor.

phrases.grammarNote: Compare English 'my head hurts' (I am subject) with Spanish 'me duele la cabeza' (la cabeza is subject) — a classic backwards verb like 'gustar'.
phrases.memoryHook: Think of the head as the one doing the hurting TO you — 'la cabeza duele a mí' shortened to 'me duele la cabeza'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: My head has hurt for three days
practiceItems.answer: Me duele la cabeza desde hace tres días

practiceItems.prompt: Me duele la ___ desde hace tres días.

phrases.target: Me duelen los pies después de caminar tanto
phrases.native: My feet hurt after walking so much
phrases.phonetic: meh DWEH-len los pee-EHS des-PWEHS deh kah-mee-NAR TAN-toh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Duelen' (plural) agrees with the plural subject 'los pies' — the verb changes number to match the body part, not the person.

exampleSentence.target: Me duelen los pies después de caminar tanto por la ciudad.
exampleSentence.native: My feet hurt after walking so much around the city.

phrases.grammarNote: Unlike English, the verb 'doler' must agree with the body part: singular 'duele' for one part, plural 'duelen' for more than one.
phrases.memoryHook: Feet come in pairs, so 'duelen' gets the plural '-en' — pair up the plural with the plural.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: My feet hurt after walking so much
practiceItems.answer: Me duelen los pies después de caminar tanto

practiceItems.prompt: Me ___ los pies después de caminar tanto.
¿Qué le duele después de caminar tanto?

phrases.target: Se me torció el tobillo al bajar la escalera
phrases.native: I twisted my ankle going down the stairs
phrases.phonetic: seh meh tor-see-OH el toh-BEE-yoh al bah-HAR lah es-kah-LEH-rah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: The accidental/unplanned 'se' (se me torció) shows the injury happened to you unintentionally, not that you deliberately twisted it.

exampleSentence.target: Se me torció el tobillo al bajar la escalera esta mañana.
exampleSentence.native: I twisted my ankle going down the stairs this morning.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Se me torció' distances you from blame — literally 'the ankle got twisted on me', framing it as something that happened, not something you did.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Se me' + verb is your 'oops, it just happened' formula for accidents.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I twisted my ankle going down the stairs
practiceItems.answer: Se me torció el tobillo al bajar la escalera

practiceItems.prompt: Se me torció el ___ al bajar la escalera.
¿Qué se le torció al bajar la escalera?

phrases.target: Llevo dos días con fiebre y tos
phrases.native: I've had a fever and cough for two days
phrases.phonetic: YEH-voh dohs DEE-as kon fee-EH-breh ee tohs
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Llevo + time + con...' is an alternative to 'desde hace' for expressing how long a condition has lasted, very common in spoken Mexican Spanish.

exampleSentence.target: Llevo dos días con fiebre y tos que no se me quita.
exampleSentence.native: I've had a fever and cough for two days that won't go away.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Llevo + [time] + con + [symptom]' literally means 'I carry [time] with [symptom]' — an idiomatic duration frame distinct from 'desde hace'.
phrases.memoryHook: Picture 'llevar' (to carry) — you've been carrying this fever around for two days.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I've had a fever and cough for two days
practiceItems.answer: Llevo dos días con fiebre y tos

practiceItems.prompt: Llevo dos días con fiebre y ___.

phrases.target: Tiene que tomar esta pastilla cada ocho horas
phrases.native: You have to take this pill every eight hours
phrases.phonetic: tee-EH-neh keh toh-MAR ES-tah pas-TEE-yah KAH-dah OH-choh OH-ras

phrases.target: Debe descansar y tomar mucha agua
phrases.native: You should rest and drink a lot of water
phrases.phonetic: DEH-beh des-kan-SAR ee toh-MAR MOO-chah AH-gwah

phrases.target: Hay que revisarle la garganta primero
phrases.native: We need to check your throat first
phrases.phonetic: AHY keh reh-vee-SAR-leh lah gar-GAN-tah pree-MEH-roh

phrases.target: Me duele el estómago después de comer
phrases.phonetic: meh DWEH-leh el es-TOH-mah-goh des-PWEHS deh koh-MEHR

phrases.native: Can you repeat the dosage for me, please?
phrases.phonetic: PWEH-deh reh-peh-TEER-meh lah DOH-sees, por fah-VOR

phrases.target: Entonces tomo una pastilla en la mañana y otra en la noche
phrases.native: So I take one pill in the morning and another at night
phrases.phonetic: en-TOHN-ses TOH-moh OO-nah pas-TEE-yah en lah mah-NYAH-nah ee OH-trah en lah NOH-cheh

dialogue.scenario: The learner visits a clinic in Mexico and describes symptoms to a doctor.
